## Notable Quotes

1. "There is no reading Kestrel while it is closing the day. There is the extract, and there is nothing else." — Hal Brenner (raw: "there is the extract" L22)
2. "Every project that has ever come through here has asked me for a live feed and every one of them has ended up on the extract." — Hal Brenner (raw: "ended up on the extract" L27)
3. "Twenty-two hundred to half two. Two batches inside that, and the second one is the one you want." — Hal Brenner (raw: "the second one is the one you want" L35)
4. "I do not decide what leaves. I decide what it costs to get it out." — Hal Brenner (raw: "I decide what it costs" L52)

## Tensions

## Stated Assumptions

- Anything either engagement builds against the policy master is building against yesterday, and the business has been operating that way since 1994 without anyone experiencing it as a limitation.

## Unstated Assumptions

- The team had been treating the extract as a technical constraint. Hal treats it as the only supported interface, which is a different thing and harder to negotiate.

## Open Questions

- [open question: member-data-retention-clock] How long can a Slalom-held extract of member data sit outside Calderwood before it has to be destroyed? | resolver: @Nadia Okonjo | blocks: whether either engagement can keep a working copy between sessions | default: we assume 30 days, delete on that basis, and find out we were wrong at audit
- [open question resolved: kestrel-extract-ownership] Who owns the nightly Kestrel extract now that two engagements read from it? | resolved: Hal owns the extract itself and will add fields to it on request, but each consuming engagement owns its own copy and its own retention — he was clear he will not hold data on anyone else's behalf

## Action Items / Memory Candidates
